prioritization.name: eval() Usage
prioritization.description: Use of eval() function which executes arbitrary code
solutions: Replace eval() with JSON.parse() for JSON parsing
Use dedicated expression parser libraries for mathematical expressions
Implement function whitelisting for dynamic function calls
Use template literals or string interpolation instead of eval
Consider using Web Workers for isolated code execution
prevention: Never use eval() with user input
Enable linter rules to detect eval() usage
Implement code review checks for eval() patterns
Use static analysis tools in CI/CD pipeline

prioritization.name: Command Injection
prioritization.description: Execution of system commands with user input

examples.vulnerable:
# Python - Dangerous
import subprocess
user_input = getUserInput()
subprocess.call(user_input, shell=True)

os.system(user_input)
examples.secure:
# Python - Safe
import subprocess
user_input = getUserInput()
subprocess.run(['ls', user_input], shell=False)

# Validate input
if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$', user_input):
    raise ValueError('Invalid input')

solutions: Never use shell=True in subprocess calls
Use list arguments instead of string commands
Validate and sanitize all user inputs

prioritization.name: SQL Injection

examples.vulnerable:
# Python - Dangerous
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + user_input + "'")

cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s" % user_input)
examples.secure:
# Python - Safe
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (user_input,))

# Using ORM
User.objects.filter(name=user_input)

solutions: Apply principle of least privilege to database users
prevention: Enable SQL query logging and monitoring
Developer training on secure database access

prioritization.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
prioritization.description: Injection of malicious scripts into web pages
solutions: Validate and sanitize on both client and server

prioritization.name: Path Traversal
prioritization.description: Access to files outside intended directory

examples.vulnerable:
# Python - Dangerous
filename = getUserInput()
with open('/var/www/' + filename, 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()
examples.secure:
# Python - Safe
import os
filename = getUserInput()
safe_path = os.path.join('/var/www', os.path.basename(filename))
if not safe_path.startswith('/var/www/'):
    raise ValueError('Invalid path')
with open(safe_path, 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

solutions: Use file access libraries with built-in security
prevention: Never concatenate user input with file paths

prioritization.name: Insecure Deserialization
prioritization.description: Untrusted data deserialization leading to code execution

examples.vulnerable:
# Python - Dangerous
import pickle
data = pickle.loads(user_input)

# JavaScript - Potentially dangerous
const data = JSON.parse(user_input);
examples.secure:
# Python - Safe
import json
data = json.loads(user_input)

# Use safe formats
import yaml
data = yaml.safe_load(user_input)

solutions: Use JSON or other safe serialization formats
